comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C9. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple experimental approaches and cell lines. Peer reviewers affirm findings as convincing, highlighting FZD5/8 substrate selectivity and Wnt-dependent internalization/degradation as novel contributions.

Perfect agreement on claims C10-C15. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights endogenous protein validation using knock-in cell lines and pharmacological approaches. Peer reviewers praise the genetic approach using CRISPR-mutated cell lines, though Reviewer 2 raises minor concern about potential V5 tag effects on activity.

Perfect agreement on claims C16-C25. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive genetic evidence from ZNRF3/RNF43 double knockout cells demonstrating FZD5/8 specificity and RSPO1 effects. Peer reviewers identify this as a key finding establishing Wnt-dependent negative regulatory loop.

Perfect agreement on claims C26-C32. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes DVL1/2/3 triple knockout data showing DVL promotes basal endocytosis but is not required for Wnt-induced degradation. All peer reviewers highlight this DVL-independence as a major novel finding that challenges previous models.

Agreement on claims C33-C40 with shared uncertainty. Both rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes C40 includes speculation about recycling lacking direct evidence. Peer Reviewer 3 specifically identifies this as 'the only weakness,' stating recycling hypothesis 'has not been directly demonstrated.' Both accept internalization data but question recycling interpretation.

Perfect agreement on claims C41-C50. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes data showing only ZNRF3/RNF43 effects are IWP-2 sensitive, indicating Wnt-dependence. Peer Reviewer 3 notes this addresses concerns about ectopic degradation by overexpressed membrane E3 ligases, supporting mechanistic specificity.

Perfect agreement on claims C51-C58. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights FZD5/8 knockout experiments demonstrating signaling specificity with selective rescue by FZD5 and differential effects on Wnt3a vs RSPO1 signaling. Peer reviewers accept FZD5/8 substrate selectivity as one of three significant findings.

Perfect agreement on claims C59-C62. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes proximity biotin labeling demonstrating Wnt-induced FZD5-RNF43 interaction with DVL-independence. Peer Reviewer 3 specifically notes authors 'clearly show' this interaction occurs without DVL, contrary to previous suggestions.

Agreement on claims C63-C65 with shared uncertainty. Both rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes C65 includes speculation about FZD5/8 recycling lacking direct evidence and C63 represents interpretation rather than direct demonstration. Peer reviewers accept overall mechanistic model but express uncertainty about recycling component, with Reviewer 3 noting it 'has not been directly demonstrated.'

OpenEval evaluated claims C66-C73 as SUPPORTED, noting these are primarily literature citations providing appropriate context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluated claims C74-C81 as SUPPORTED, identifying these as established background knowledge appropriately cited from literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.
